newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday due to a new issue and a new listing on the domestic A share market, which attracted funds from the repo market, traders said.

Combined turnover rose sharply to 10.52 million lots from 6.70 million, with investors pulling money out of the repo market to buy new shares and trade on the share market, traders said. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of T-bills.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.86 percent from 11.19 percent last Friday.
"But the rates rose only slightly today, with many investors having already borrowed before the weekend," one trader.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed due to weak market sentiment, traders said. The 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, the market barometre, was the most active contract today, closing down at 120.68 yuan from 121.33.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.45 million lots from 1.67 million.
"Investor confidence was weak after the market had been on a downtrend for two weeks," a trader said. "Profit-taking set in today after a short-lived technical rebound last Friday."
